extracted.intended_audience: students, legislators, jurists and readers of political philosophy interested in constitutional design and the relation of laws to national character
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating how constitutions and laws should distribute legislative, executive and judicial powers, how that distribution affects liberty, and how laws must fit national spirit, climate and customs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of the three powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Il faut que... quelle est la distribution des trois pouvoirs, et calculer par là les degrés de liberté dont chacun d'eux peut jouir (how legislative, executive and judicial powers are distributed and balanced to secure liberty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the balance among people, senate and magistrates as the criterion: a well-distributed constitution balances powers so no single element dominates. Examples: Rome's mix (people strong in legislation, senate strong in execution and part in legislation/judging) preserved liberty; upsetting this balance (e.g., Gracchi reforms) destroyed constitutional equilibrium and produced large harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular retention of election and confirmation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In a republic the people should retain key rights: electing magistrates and confirming acts (the people reserved the right to elect magistrates and to confirm the acts of the senate and generals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting institutions, ensure the populace retains sufficient formal powers (elections, confirmations, appeals) to check other branches; Roman example shows people surrendered most executive power but kept election/confirmation as a restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate control over finances and foreign affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The senate ought to have disposition of public monies, grant revenues, arbitrate allied affairs, decide war and peace, and direct consuls (senate disposed of public funds, gave revenues to farm, decided war and peace, fixed troop numbers, distributed provinces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to a deliberative council key fiscal and foreign-policy powers to moderate popular impulses and provide continuity; Montesquieu cites Rome where senate's control of resources and foreign policy gave it balancing weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of judicial functions: fact versus law
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish questions of fact (decided by judges chosen for each case) from questions of law (referred to a court of law or special tribunal) (les juges ne décidaient que des questions de fait; pour les questions de droit elles étaient portées au tribunal des centumvirs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design courts so lay or ad hoc judges resolve facts, while trained legal tribunals handle legal doctrine; reduces misuse of legal expertise and preserves fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge selection by consent of the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing judges with the consent of the parties is favorable to liberty (le préteur prenait les juges du consentement des parties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, allow parties a role in selecting fact-finders to reduce bias and increase acceptance of outcomes; Montesquieu notes this practice in Rome and compares it to English recusation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term and case-by-case judicial appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges were not even for a year; they were taken for each affair (les juges n'étaient pas même pour un an, puisqu'on les prenait pour chaque affaire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary, ad hoc appointment of judges for individual cases can protect liberty by limiting entrenched judicial power. Use with caution balancing consistency and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit executive power over life by allowing appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Valerienne law permitted appeals to the people from consul ordinances that endangered a citizen's life; consuls could not pronounce capital punishment against a Roman without the people's will (les consuls ne purent plus prononcer une peine capitale contre un citoyen romain que par la volonté du peuple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrain executive criminal authority (especially capital punishment) by procedural rights of appeal or popular review to prevent arbitrary despotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentrating all three powers in distant governors
rubrics_metrics.description: When magistrates are sent to provinces they often hold united executive, legislative and judicial power, becoming despotic (les magistrats envoyés avaient une puissance qui réunissait celle de toutes les magistratures; c'étaient des magistrats despotiques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should prevent remote governors from exercising unchecked triple power; provide oversight, rotation, or institutional separation to avoid provincial tyranny and abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation proportional to share in government
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxation should be proportioned to the share each citizen has in the government (Servius Tullius divided citizens in classes and fixed share of tax proportional to their part in government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create tax systems aligned with political enfranchisement so burdens correspond to political voice; this linkage promotes perceived equity and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not entrust judicial power to those with financial interests (publicani/chevaliers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving judgements to the chevaliers (tax-farmers/contractors) produced rapine and abuse in the provinces (les chevaliers, comme les plus riches, formaient la cavalerie... quand à Rome les jugements furent transportés aux traitants, il n'y eut plus de vertu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflict-of-interest by excluding those whose livelihood depends on state contracting or profiteering from judicial offices; such assignment breeds corruption, social disorder and rebellion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial composition should help balance political powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking judges from the knights (chevaliers) rather than senators removed the senate's part in judging and weakened constitutional balance (les Gracques privèrent les sénateurs de la puissance de juger... le sénat ne put plus résister).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the social composition of courts to maintain checks among governing orders; transferring judicial authority between social classes can alter political equilibria and should be considered deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare public spirit before imposing laws
rubrics_metrics.description: For the best laws it is necessary that minds be prepared; laws which shock the manners of a nation are intolerable (pour les meilleures lois, il est nécessaire que les esprits soient préparés).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawmakers should account for public dispositions and cultural readiness; sudden imposition of alien institutions can produce rejection or perverse effects. Gradual reform and cultivation of public opinion are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt laws to climate, religion, moeurs and national 'esprit général'
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws must relate to the climate, religion, maxims of government, examples, moeurs and manners from which a nation's general spirit results (les lois ont du rapport avec le climat, la religion, les maximes du gouvernement, les moeurs et les manières).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing legal rules, account for geographic/climatic conditions and prevailing customs and beliefs; uniform transplant of laws across disparate societies can fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize two kinds of tyranny: real and of opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two sorts of tyranny: a real one (violence of government) and one of opinion (when rulers establish things that shock a nation's way of thinking) (Il y a deux sortes de tyrannie: une réelle... et une d'opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies not only for coercive power but also for cultural legitimacy; laws that deeply offend national manners can function tyrannically even without overt violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slavery is unjust by natural and civil law
rubrics_metrics.description: The supposed juridical origins of slavery (prisoners of war, sale, birth) are unsound; slavery is not good by nature and is harmful to both master and slave (L'esclavage proprement dit... il n'est pas bon par sa nature; il n'est utile ni au maître ni à l'esclave).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or drafting laws on servitude, consider moral and natural-law objections: slavery provides no reciprocal legal benefit to the enslaved and is incompatible with humane and civic virtues; historical justifications should be critically examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerability of slavery depends on regime and climate
rubrics_metrics.description: In despotic countries slavery is more tolerable because subjects already lack freedom; in monarchies, democracies and aristocracies slavery is contrary to the spirit of the constitution (dans les pays despotiques... l'esclavage civil est plus tolérable; dans le gouvernement monarchique il ne faut point d'esclaves; dans la démocratie et l'aristocratie des esclaves sont contre l'esprit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fit of institution of slavery with regime type and broader moral-political aims; even if pragmatic arguments are made, they conflict with the ethos of non-despotic constitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different jurisdictions for public versus private crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish crimes that concern citizens among themselves (private) from those that concern the state (public); people judge public crimes, private crimes pursued by appointed quaestors (Le peuple jugea les crimes publics; à l'égard des privés, il nomma pour chaque crime un questeur pour en faire la poursuite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate prosecutorial and adjudicative responsibilities according to whether offenses primarily harm citizens or the state; use special commissions or appointed prosecutors for private crimes to structure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialize criminal jurisdiction with permanent commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some criminal commissions were made permanent and specific praetors were given jurisdiction for categories of crimes (quelques-unes de ces commissions furent rendues permanentes... on créa divers préteurs et on attribua à chacun d'eux quelqu'une de ces questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider permanent or specialized magistracies for recurring criminal matters to improve expertise and consistency, while monitoring risks of entrenchment and abuse.
